content: Thermo Fisher Scientific is a prominent company in the life sciences sector, established in 2006 through the merger of Thermo Electron and Fisher Scientific. Thermo Electron was founded in 1956 by George Hatsopoulos, who held a PhD in mechanical engineering from MIT. The company specialized in providing analytical and laboratory products and services, achieving revenues exceeding $2 billion by 2004. Fisher Scientific, on the other hand, was established in 1902 by Chester G. Fisher. It focused on supplying laboratory equipment, chemicals, and other materials essential for healthcare, scientific research, safety, and education. On May 14, 2006, Thermo Electron and Fisher Scientific announced their intention to merge in a tax-free, stock-for-stock exchange. The resulting entity was named Thermo Fisher Scientific. By November 9, 2006, the merger was officially completed. However, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) determined that the acquisition was anticompetitive in the market for centrifugal evaporators. As a result, Fisher Scientific was required to divest its subsidiary, Genevac. In April 2007, Genevac was sold to Riverlake Equity Partners LP, and the merger subsequently received FTC approval. Currently, Thermo Fisher Scientific markets its products under the brand names Thermo Scientific and Fisher Scientific. According to company data, 46% of its sales are derived from life sciences, 20% from healthcare, and 34% from industrial, environmental, and safety sectors.
